title: Covey plugin catalogue entry
description: One file per plugin under plugins/. The artefact itself lives elsewhere and is pinned by digest.

name.description: Plugin identity. Must equal the filename stem and the name inside the artefact. Also the credential prefix (<name>_token/<name>_url) and the guard-rail subject prefix.

description.description: One sentence: what an agent can do with this system.

category.description: Placement in the store. Purely classification — no behaviour depends on it.

kind.description: custom = JSON manifest, mcp = MCP server configuration, wasm = a WebAssembly module (real code, sandboxed: no sockets, no filesystem, and it never sees the credential), builtin = compiled into Covey (listed for findability, activated rather than installed).

publisher.description: Who publishes it. Stable across a publisher's plugins.

homepage.description: Where the source and the issue tracker live.

license.description: SPDX identifier of the plugin (not of this index).

icon.description: The plugin's mark, EMBEDDED as a base64 data: URI — never a link to an image on a server. A remote image would fire a request to that host for everyone who opens a store page in every instance reading this catalogue: a counting pixel nobody asked for. Covey drops anything else and falls back to a category symbol, so an omitted or malformed icon costs nothing but the logo.

deprecated.description: Present = the plugin is no longer maintained; the text says what to use instead. It stays in the catalogue, marked, so existing installations keep resolving.

versions.description: Newest first. Append-only: a published version is never edited.

version.description: Semantic version of the plugin, unique within this entry.

url.description: Immutable URL of the artefact — a tag or commit, never a branch.

sha256.description: Digest of the artefact. Verified in CI and again at install time.

covey_min_version.description: Oldest Covey release that can interpret this artefact.

notes.description: What changed. Shown next to the update button.

build.description: How this artefact is built from source. REQUIRED for kind=wasm, and the reason is the whole trust story: a reviewer can read a manifest, but nobody reviews a multi-megabyte binary. CI checks out repo at ref, builds with the named Go version and -trimpath, and refuses the entry unless the result matches sha256 exactly. Go's wasm output is byte-identical across machines and paths under those conditions, so this turns 'trust the publisher' into 'read the source'.

repo.description: Clonable URL of the source repository.

ref.description: Tag or commit SHA — immutable, like the artefact URL.

dir.description: Package directory inside the repository. Default: the root.

go.description: Go version to build with. A different toolchain produces different bytes, so this is part of what is being pinned.

builtin_since.description: kind=builtin only: the Covey release from which this plugin ships compiled in.
